answer: Identity creation draws a rising toll from one operator purse. The first key prepays a small slice, and each later key must prepay every earlier slice again plus a new one, so the bill bends into a spiral instead of repeating. Fresh addresses can wander all they like; the purse still sees the same operator. A comet of signups inside one hour steepens that curve, because the toll follows the count in that hour, not the label on the key.
